details:
Connect any standard Bluetooth headset to an Android device.Launch VRChat mobile.Unfocus the app briefly (or toggle the Quick Menu/Notification Shade) to trigger the known Bluetooth disconnection bug.Instead of a silent disconnect, the audio stream catches in an infinite buffer loop, generating an immediate high-decibel digital scream directly into the headphones.

Bypasses Android Volume Caps: The resulting digital feedback loop completely ignores system media volume restrictions. It blasts at maximum hardware output even if the user has their phone volume set to low.Risk of Permanent Acoustic Trauma: Because wireless earbuds sit directly inside the ear canal, this sudden, ultra-loud feedback loop is actively exposing mobile users to acoustic shock and persistent tinnitus.Neurological Distress & Migraines: The violent, unexpected nature of the high-decibel screeching causes immediate physical distress, with multiple users reporting the onset of severe migraines, nausea, and tension headaches directly following the audio blast.

This is no longer just a minor device-compatibility issue; it is a physical safety liability. The engineering team must prioritize fixing the underlying Unity-to-Android audio routing code immediately to prevent further acoustic exposure and physical injury to the user base.
title: [CRITICAL SAFETY HAZARD] High-Decibel Audio Buffer Loop causing Acoustic Shock and Migraines on Android Bluetooth
